Updaters and value trackers

Source: vignettes/updaters.Rmd
updaters.Rmd

An animation describes a change from a start to an end. An updater describes a rule instead: a function attached to a mobject that runs on every frame and adjusts the mobject, for example “stay above that dot” or “turn a little”. Updaters keep running during animations and during self$wait(), which makes them the tool for labels that follow things, continuous motion, and anything driven by a changing number. A ValueTracker holds such a number.

This vignette assumes you know how to write a scene and play animations; see Animations for that.

Updaters on mobjects

Updaters without time

mob$add_updater(f) attaches a function f(m), called on every frame with the mobject itself. The label below has an updater that keeps it above the dot, so it follows the dot through every animation without being animated itself.

FollowTheDot <- R6::R6Class("FollowTheDot", inherit = Scene,
  public = list(construct = function() {
    dot <- Dot(LEFT * 4, radius = 0.15, color = YELLOW)
    label <- Text("follow me", font_size = 32)
    label$add_updater(function(m) m$next_to(dot, UP))
    self$add(dot, label)
    self$play(dot$animate$shift(RIGHT * 4 + UP * 1.5))
    self$play(dot$animate$shift(RIGHT * 4 + DOWN * 3), run_time = 1.5)
    self$wait(0.3)
  })
)

add_updater() returns the mobject, so it chains. Two more arguments control it: call_updater = TRUE runs the function once right away, which puts the label in place before the first frame, and index inserts the updater at a position in the list of updaters (they run in order). mob$get_updaters() returns the list.

Updaters with time

If the function has an argument named dt, it is a time based updater, called as f(m, dt) with the time in seconds since the previous frame. Multiplying a rate by dt gives motion at a constant speed that does not depend on the frame rate. The argument has to be called dt: that name, not the number of arguments, tells manimR to pass the time.

DtUpdater <- R6::R6Class("DtUpdater", inherit = Scene,
  public = list(construct = function() {
    square <- Square(color = BLUE, fill_opacity = 0.5)$shift(LEFT * 3)
    square$add_updater(function(m, dt) m$rotate(PI / 2 * dt))
    dot <- Dot(RIGHT * 1, radius = 0.15, color = ORANGE)
    dot$add_updater(function(m, dt) m$shift(RIGHT * 1.5 * dt))
    self$add(square, dot)
    self$wait(2)
  })
)

A scene with time based updaters keeps rendering new frames during self$wait(), while a scene without them just repeats a still frame. self$pause() always holds a still frame and does not run updaters.

Removing, clearing and suspending updaters

  • mob$remove_updater(f) removes one updater. It has to be the same function object that was added, so store the function in a variable first.
  • mob$clear_updaters() removes all updaters of the mobject and its submobjects.
  • mob$suspend_updating() pauses the updaters without removing them, and mob$resume_updating() turns them back on (and runs them once).
dot <- Dot()
drift <- function(m, dt) m$shift(RIGHT * dt)
dot$add_updater(drift)
length(dot$get_updaters())
#> [1] 1
dot$has_time_based_updater()
#> [1] TRUE
dot$remove_updater(drift)
length(dot$get_updaters())
#> [1] 0

The label below stops following the dot while its updaters are suspended and jumps back when they resume. Then the updater is removed for good.

SuspendResume <- R6::R6Class("SuspendResume", inherit = Scene,
  public = list(construct = function() {
    dot <- Dot(LEFT * 3, radius = 0.15, color = YELLOW)
    label <- Text("label", font_size = 32)
    stay_above <- function(m) m$next_to(dot, UP)
    label$add_updater(stay_above, call_updater = TRUE)
    self$add(dot, label)
    self$play(dot$animate$shift(RIGHT * 2))
    label$suspend_updating()
    self$play(dot$animate$shift(DOWN * 1.5))
    label$resume_updating()
    self$wait(0.3)
    label$remove_updater(stay_above)
    self$play(dot$animate$shift(RIGHT * 3))
    self$wait(0.3)
  })
)

Animations also suspend updaters: while an animation plays, the updaters of the mobject it animates are paused (and resumed at the end), so the updater and the animation do not fight over the mobject. Pass suspend_mobject_updating = FALSE to the animation to keep them running.

Value trackers

A ValueTracker is an invisible mobject that stores one number. Read it with get_value() and change it with set_value() or increment_value(). Because it is a mobject, $animate animates the number smoothly from its current value to the new one.

tracker <- ValueTracker(1)
tracker$get_value()
#> [1] 1
tracker$set_value(3)
tracker$increment_value(0.5)
tracker$get_value()
#> [1] 3.5

The usual pattern is: keep the state in a tracker, give the mobjects updaters that read it, and animate the tracker. Here a pointer and a number follow a tracker along a number line. DecimalNumber() normally typesets its digits with LaTeX; mob_class = Text uses system fonts instead, so this example runs without LaTeX.

TrackerNumberLine <- R6::R6Class("TrackerNumberLine", inherit = Scene,
  public = list(construct = function() {
    line <- NumberLine(x_range = c(-5, 5, 1), length = 10)
    tracker <- ValueTracker(0)
    pointer <- Triangle(color = YELLOW, fill_opacity = 1)$scale(0.15)$rotate(PI)
    pointer$add_updater(function(m) m$next_to(line$n2p(tracker$get_value()), UP), call_updater = TRUE)
    number <- DecimalNumber(0, num_decimal_places = 2, mob_class = Text, font_size = 36)
    number$add_updater(function(m) m$set_value(tracker$get_value())$next_to(pointer, UP), call_updater = TRUE)
    self$add(line, pointer, number)
    self$play(tracker$animate$set_value(4))
    self$play(tracker$animate$increment_value(-6.5), run_time = 1.5)
    tracker$set_value(-1)
    self$wait(0.3)
    self$play(tracker$animate(rate_func = there_and_back)$set_value(2), run_time = 1.5)
    self$wait(0.3)
  })
)

Setting the value directly (tracker$set_value(-1) above) jumps; the updaters pick up the new value on the next frame.

Arithmetic on a tracker works on its value and returns a new tracker for +, -, *, / and ^, and a plain value for comparisons:

a <- ValueTracker(2)
(a * 3)$get_value()
#> [1] 6
a > 1
#> [1] TRUE

Upstream manim’s in place operators such as tracker += 1 have no R equivalent; use tracker$increment_value(1).

ComplexValueTracker stores a complex number, handy for points in the plane: Re() and Im() of its value are the coordinates.

ComplexTracker <- R6::R6Class("ComplexTracker", inherit = Scene,
  public = list(construct = function() {
    plane <- NumberPlane(x_range = c(-4, 4, 1), y_range = c(-3, 3, 1))
    z <- ComplexValueTracker(-3 + 2i)
    dot <- Dot(radius = 0.15, color = YELLOW)
    dot$add_updater(function(m) m$move_to(c(Re(z$get_value()), Im(z$get_value()), 0)), call_updater = TRUE)
    self$add(plane, dot)
    self$play(z$animate$set_value(3 - 1i))
    self$play(z$animate$set_value(z$get_value() * 1i), run_time = 1.5)
    self$wait(0.3)
  })
)

Updater helpers

always_redraw()

always_redraw(f) takes a function with no arguments that builds a mobject, calls it once, and adds an updater that rebuilds the mobject from scratch on every frame. It is the simplest way to draw something that depends on other moving mobjects, such as a line between two dots.

AlwaysRedraw <- R6::R6Class("AlwaysRedraw", inherit = Scene,
  public = list(construct = function() {
    a <- Dot(LEFT * 3 + DOWN, radius = 0.15, color = BLUE)
    b <- Dot(RIGHT * 3 + UP, radius = 0.15, color = ORANGE)
    link <- always_redraw(function() Line(a$get_center(), b$get_center(), color = YELLOW))
    brace <- always_redraw(function() Brace(link, direction = DOWN, color = GREY))
    self$add(link, brace, a, b)
    self$play(a$animate$shift(UP * 2.5 + RIGHT), b$animate$shift(DOWN * 2))
    self$play(Rotate(b, angle = PI / 2, about_point = ORIGIN), run_time = 1.5)
    self$wait(0.3)
  })
)

Rebuilding is slower than adjusting an existing mobject, so prefer a plain updater when a method call such as move_to() or next_to() is enough.

always(), f_always() and $always

  • always(mob$method, ...) calls the method with the same arguments on every frame. always(label$next_to, dot, UP) is shorthand for label$add_updater(function(m) m$next_to(dot, UP)).
  • mob$always$method(...) does the same with upstream manim’s syntax (label.always.next_to(dot, UP)), and also calls the method once right away.
  • f_always(mob$method, ...) passes functions with no arguments; each is called on every frame to produce the argument. Use it when the argument itself changes, such as a point read from a tracker. Named arguments are passed as they are.

always_shift() and always_rotate()

always_shift(mob, direction, rate) moves a mobject at rate units per second and always_rotate(mob, rate, ...) turns it at rate radians per second (further arguments such as about_point go to rotate()). Both add a time based updater and return the mobject.

AlwaysHelpers <- R6::R6Class("AlwaysHelpers", inherit = Scene,
  public = list(construct = function() {
    x <- ValueTracker(-4)
    dot <- Dot(radius = 0.15, color = YELLOW)
    f_always(dot$move_to, function() c(x$get_value(), -2, 0))
    label <- Text("f_always", font_size = 28)
    always(label$next_to, dot, UP)
    square <- Square(side_length = 1.2, color = BLUE)$shift(LEFT * 3 + UP * 1.5)
    always_rotate(square, rate = PI / 2)
    star <- Star(outer_radius = 0.5, color = ORANGE)$shift(RIGHT * 1 + UP * 1.5)
    always_shift(star, direction = RIGHT, rate = 1)
    tag <- Text("always_shift", font_size = 24)
    tag$always$next_to(star, DOWN)
    self$add(dot, label, square, star, tag)
    self$play(x$animate$set_value(4), run_time = 2)
    self$wait(0.3)
  })
)

Animations as updaters

turn_animation_into_updater(anim) plays an animation through an updater on its mobject instead of through self$play(), so it runs alongside whatever else happens, starting after delay seconds. With cycle = TRUE, or with the shortcut cycle_animation(anim), it restarts whenever it ends. The scene keeps playing it during self$wait().

AnimationUpdater <- R6::R6Class("AnimationUpdater", inherit = Scene,
  public = list(construct = function() {
    once <- Square(color = BLUE, fill_opacity = 0.5)$shift(LEFT * 3)
    looping <- Circle(color = ORANGE)$shift(RIGHT * 3)
    turn_animation_into_updater(Rotate(once, angle = PI / 4, run_time = 1), delay = 0.5)
    cycle_animation(Indicate(looping, run_time = 1))
    self$add(once, looping)
    self$wait(2)
    self$wait(0.5)
  })
)

Animations that run functions

Three animations run a function on every frame, but only while they play, so they work like temporary updaters:

  • UpdateFromFunc(mob, f) calls f(mob).
  • UpdateFromAlphaFunc(mob, f) calls f(mob, alpha), with alpha going from 0 to 1 through the animation’s rate function. Make f set properties to absolute values, since it runs on every frame.
  • MaintainPositionRelativeTo(mob, tracked) keeps mob at the same offset from tracked as when the animation started.
UpdateFromFuncExample <- R6::R6Class("UpdateFromFuncExample", inherit = Scene,
  public = list(construct = function() {
    dot <- Dot(LEFT * 4 + UP * 1.5, radius = 0.15, color = YELLOW)
    label <- Text("UpdateFromFunc", font_size = 28)$next_to(dot, UP)
    square <- Square(color = BLUE)$shift(LEFT * 3 + DOWN * 1.5)
    box <- Square(side_length = 0.8, color = ORANGE)$shift(RIGHT * 1 + DOWN * 1.5)
    tag <- Text("MaintainPositionRelativeTo", font_size = 24)$next_to(box, UP)
    self$add(dot, label, square, box, tag)
    self$play(
      dot$animate$shift(RIGHT * 8),
      UpdateFromFunc(label, function(m) m$next_to(dot, UP)),
      UpdateFromAlphaFunc(square, function(m, alpha) m$set_fill(BLUE, opacity = alpha)),
      box$animate$shift(RIGHT * 3),
      MaintainPositionRelativeTo(tag, box),
      run_time = 2
    )
    self$wait(0.3)
  })
)

Traced paths and animated boundaries

TracedPath(f) is a line that grows on every frame by the point returned by f(), a function with no arguments such as dot$get_center. With dissipating_time, the oldest part disappears after that many seconds, which leaves a short tail.

AnimatedBoundary(vmob) draws an outline around a VMobject that keeps redrawing itself in cycling colors, cycle_rate cycles per second. Both are mobjects with built in time based updaters: add them to the scene and they run by themselves.

AnimatedBoundaryExample <- R6::R6Class("AnimatedBoundaryExample", inherit = Scene,
  public = list(construct = function() {
    word <- Text("Animated boundary", font_size = 60)
    boundary <- AnimatedBoundary(word, colors = c(RED, GREEN, BLUE), cycle_rate = 3)
    self$add(word, boundary)
    self$wait(1)
    self$play(word$animate$set_color(YELLOW))
    self$wait(1)
  })
)

Scene updaters and wait_until()

A scene can have updaters too: self$add_updater(f) registers a function f(dt) of the time step only, called once per frame after the mobject updaters; self$remove_updater(f) removes it. Use it for state that belongs to the scene rather than to one mobject.

self$wait_until(stop_condition, max_time = 60) waits until the function stop_condition() returns TRUE, checking it on every frame, or until max_time seconds have passed. It is the same as self$wait(max_time, stop_condition = stop_condition). Use it when the length of a wait depends on what the updaters do.

The comet below moves along a circle by reading an angle that a scene updater advances, leaves a dissipating trail, and the scene waits until it has gone around one and a half times.

Comet <- R6::R6Class("Comet", inherit = Scene,
  public = list(construct = function() {
    angle <- ValueTracker(0)
    self$add_updater(function(dt) angle$increment_value(PI * dt))
    comet <- Dot(radius = 0.12, color = YELLOW)
    comet$add_updater(function(m) {
      m$move_to(2.5 * c(cos(angle$get_value()), sin(angle$get_value()), 0))
    }, call_updater = TRUE)
    trail <- TracedPath(comet$get_center, stroke_color = YELLOW, stroke_width = 4, dissipating_time = 0.6)
    self$add(Dot(radius = 0.3, color = ORANGE), comet, trail)
    self$wait_until(function() angle$get_value() >= 3 * PI, max_time = 5)
  })
)

Numbers that follow values

DecimalNumber() (and Integer() for whole numbers) can be updated with set_value(), which redraws the digits while keeping the edge given by edge_to_fix in place. In an updater this gives a live readout. Its formatting arguments include num_decimal_places, include_sign, group_with_commas, unit (LaTeX appended after the number, such as "^\\circ"), and show_ellipsis.

The examples in this section use the default LaTeX digits, so they need a LaTeX installation.

A dot on a graph with a live label

The classic: a value tracker for x, a dot redrawn on the graph at x, and a number showing sin(x) that rides along with the dot.

GraphDotLabel <- R6::R6Class("GraphDotLabel", inherit = Scene,
  public = list(construct = function() {
    axes <- Axes(x_range = c(-4, 4, 1), y_range = c(-1.5, 1.5, 0.5), x_length = 11, y_length = 5)
    graph <- axes$plot(function(x) sin(x), color = BLUE)
    x <- ValueTracker(-4)
    dot <- always_redraw(function() Dot(axes$i2gp(x$get_value(), graph), radius = 0.1, color = YELLOW))
    value <- DecimalNumber(sin(-4), num_decimal_places = 2, include_sign = TRUE, font_size = 36)
    value$add_updater(function(m) m$set_value(sin(x$get_value()))$next_to(dot, UP), call_updater = TRUE)
    self$add(axes, graph, dot, value)
    self$play(x$animate$set_value(4), run_time = 3, rate_func = linear)
    self$wait(0.3)
  })
)

Variable()

Variable(value, label) packages the pattern: a label, an equals sign and a number driven by its own tracker, stored in $tracker. Animate the tracker to change the number. var_type = "integer" shows whole numbers.

VariableExample <- R6::R6Class("VariableExample", inherit = Scene,
  public = list(construct = function() {
    x <- Variable(0.5, "x", num_decimal_places = 3)$shift(UP)
    n <- Variable(1, "n", var_type = "integer")$next_to(x, DOWN, aligned_edge = LEFT)
    self$add(x, n)
    self$play(x$tracker$animate$set_value(2.718), n$tracker$animate$set_value(100), run_time = 2)
    self$wait(0.3)
  })
)

To count a number without a tracker, use the ChangeDecimalToValue() and ChangingDecimal() animations from Animations.

Two more classics

A clock

A time based updater turns the hand at a constant rate, a quarter turn per second, for as long as the scene runs.

Clock <- R6::R6Class("Clock", inherit = Scene,
  public = list(construct = function() {
    face <- Circle(radius = 2.5, color = WHITE)
    ticks <- VGroup(lapply(0:11, function(i) {
      Line(UP * 2.2, UP * 2.5)$rotate(-i * TAU / 12, about_point = ORIGIN)
    }))
    hand <- Line(ORIGIN, UP * 2, color = RED, stroke_width = 6)
    hand$add_updater(function(m, dt) m$rotate(-TAU / 4 * dt, about_point = ORIGIN))
    self$add(face, ticks, hand, Dot(radius = 0.1))
    self$wait(3)
  })
)

A rolling circle

A wheel rolls along the ground: its updater shifts it forward and turns it by the matching angle (distance over radius), and a traced path follows a point on the rim, drawing a cycloid. The scene waits until the wheel reaches the right side, then removes the updater so it stops.

RollingCircle <- R6::R6Class("RollingCircle", inherit = Scene,
  public = list(construct = function() {
    r <- 0.7
    speed <- 2.5
    ground <- Line(LEFT * 7, RIGHT * 7, color = GREY)$shift(DOWN * 2)
    circle <- Circle(radius = r, color = BLUE)$move_to(c(-5.5, -2 + r, 0))
    spoke <- Line(circle$get_center(), circle$get_bottom(), color = BLUE)
    rim_point <- Dot(circle$get_bottom(), radius = 0.08, color = YELLOW)
    wheel <- VGroup(circle, spoke, rim_point)
    wheel$add_updater(function(m, dt) {
      center <- circle$get_center()
      m$rotate(-speed * dt / r, about_point = center)
      m$shift(RIGHT * speed * dt)
    })
    trace <- TracedPath(rim_point$get_center, stroke_color = YELLOW, stroke_width = 3)
    self$add(ground, wheel, trace)
    self$wait_until(function() circle$get_x() >= 5.5, max_time = 6)
    wheel$clear_updaters()
    self$wait(0.3)
  })
)

Updaters and speed changes

ChangeSpeed() plays an animation faster or slower in parts. Ordinary updaters keep their own pace; an updater added with change_speed_add_updater(mob, f) speeds up and slows down together with the animation. See Animations for an example.
